yvowels.title: Y-vowels
yvowels.concept: Adding a short stroke makes a **y**-sound: ㅏ → ㅑ (ya), ㅓ → ㅕ (yeo), ㅗ → ㅛ (yo), ㅜ → ㅠ (yu). ㅐ (ae) and ㅔ (e) sound very similar in modern Korean.

consonants2.title: More consonants
consonants2.concept: ㄹ is between “r” and “l”. ㅈ (j), ㅊ (ch, with a puff of air), ㅋ (k, with a puff of air), ㅌ (t, with a puff of air) and ㅍ (p, with a puff of air) complete the basic consonants.

doubled.title: Doubled consonants
doubled.concept: ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ, ㅆ and ㅉ are tense sounds: say them with a tight throat and no puff of air, like the first sound in “skate”.

batchim.title: Final consonants
batchim.concept: A consonant under the syllable is called **받침 (batchim)**. It closes the syllable: 안 (an), 말 (mal), 밤 (bam), 강 (gang), 집 (jip), 책 (chaek). Only seven sounds are possible at the end: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅇ.

words2.title: Everyday words
words2.concept: Read each word syllable by syllable. 학교 is read “hakgyo”: the final ㄱ of 학 is closed and the next syllable is pronounced tightly.

words3.title: Words about the world
words3.concept: People and nature: 사람 (person), 나라 (country), 하늘 (sky), 산 (mountain), 강 (river), 꽃 (flower).

manners.title: Polite expressions
manners.concept: Use 실례합니다 to get someone's attention or pass by, 고마워요 to thank someone in a friendly way, 천만에요 to answer thanks, and 축하해요 to congratulate.

introduce.title: Names and countries
introduce.concept: Ask a name with 이름이 뭐예요? and a country with 어느 나라 사람이에요? Answer with 제 이름은 ___예요 or 저는 ___ 사람이에요.

partings.title: Saying goodbye
partings.concept: Among friends you can say 잘 가요 (goodbye), 내일 봐요 (see you tomorrow), 또 만나요 (see you again) and 잘 자요 (sleep well).

wellbeing.title: How are you?
wellbeing.concept: Ask 잘 지냈어요? (Have you been well?) and answer 잘 지내요 (I'm doing well). 좋은 아침이에요 means “It's a good morning.”

helpme.title: Asking for help
helpme.concept: Say 도와주세요 to ask for help, 모르겠어요 when you do not know, 알겠어요 when you understand, and 다시 말해 주세요 to ask someone to say it again.

opinions.title: Likes and answers
opinions.concept: 좋아요 means good or fine, 싫어요 means you don't like it, 맞아요 means “that's right” and 틀려요 means “that's wrong”.

native10.title: Native numbers 6–10
native10.concept: Continue the native Korean numbers: 여섯 (6), 일곱 (7), 여덟 (8), 아홉 (9), 열 (10).

sino.title: Sino-Korean numbers
sino.concept: Sino-Korean numbers: 일 (1), 이 (2), 삼 (3), 사 (4), 오 (5), 육 (6), 칠 (7), 팔 (8), 구 (9), 십 (10). They are used for money, dates, phone numbers and minutes.

ages.title: Age
ages.concept: Ask 몇 살이에요? (How old are you?). Ages use native numbers plus 살: 열 살 (10 years old), 스무 살 (20), 서른 살 (30).

family2.title: More family words
family2.concept: Siblings use different words depending on who is speaking: a woman says 오빠 (older brother) and 언니 (older sister). Also 아들 (son), 딸 (daughter), 부모님 (parents).

ourfamily.title: Our family
ourfamily.concept: Koreans often say 우리 (we, our) instead of “my”: 우리 가족 means “my family”. Count people with 명: 네 명 (four people).

food.title: Food and drink
food.concept: 밥 (rice, a meal), 빵 (bread), 과일 (fruit), 고기 (meat), 물 (water), 우유 (milk).

likes.title: Likes and dislikes
likes.concept: Say what you like with -를/을 좋아해요 and what you don't like with -를/을 싫어해요: 저는 사과를 좋아해요.

adjectives.title: Describing things
adjectives.concept: Describing words also end in -요: 커요 (big), 작아요 (small), 많아요 (many), 맛있어요 (delicious), 예뻐요 (pretty).

weather.title: Weather
weather.concept: 날씨 (weather), 더워요 (it's hot), 추워요 (it's cold), 비가 와요 (it's raining), 눈이 와요 (it's snowing).

negation.title: Saying no with 안 and 못
negation.concept: Put **안** before a verb to say you don't do something (안 가요). Put **못** before it to say you can't (못 가요).

daily.title: Daily routine
daily.concept: 일어나요 (wake up), 씻어요 (wash), 일해요 (work), 자요 (sleep). Time words such as 아침 (morning) and 밤 (night) take 에: 아침에.

weekdays.title: Days of the week
weekdays.concept: 월요일 (Mon), 화요일 (Tue), 수요일 (Wed), 목요일 (Thu), 금요일 (Fri), 토요일 (Sat), 일요일 (Sun).

months.title: Months
months.concept: Months are a Sino-Korean number plus 월: 일월 (January), 삼월 (March), 오월 (May), 칠월 (July), 구월 (September), 십이월 (December).

clock.title: Telling the hour
clock.concept: Hours use native numbers plus 시: 한 시 (1:00), 두 시 (2:00), 세 시 (3:00), 열 시 (10:00). Ask 몇 시예요?

frequency.title: How often
frequency.concept: 매일 (every day), 자주 (often), 가끔 (sometimes), 항상 (always). Place them before the verb.

past2.title: More past tense
past2.concept: The past ending is -았/었어요: 했어요 (did), 왔어요 (came), 만났어요 (met), 샀어요 (bought), 잤어요 (slept).

birthday.title: Birthdays and weekends
birthday.concept: 생일 (birthday), 주말 (weekend), 선물 (gift). Ask 생일이 언제예요? and answer 제 생일은 오월이에요.

restaurant.title: At a restaurant
restaurant.concept: 메뉴 (menu), 주문할게요 (I'll order), 물 더 주세요 (more water, please), 계산해 주세요 (the bill, please).

transport.title: Getting around
transport.concept: 버스 (bus), 지하철 (subway), 택시 (taxi), 기차 (train). Say how you go with -로/으로: 버스로 가요.

phone.title: Phone calls and messages
phone.concept: 전화 (phone call), 전화번호 (phone number), 문자 (text message). 전화해요 means “I call”.

hospital.title: At the hospital
hospital.concept: 병원 (hospital), 약 (medicine), 아파요 (it hurts). Say the body part first: 머리가 아파요 (my head hurts).

requests.title: Polite requests
requests.concept: -세요 and -아/어 주세요 make polite requests: 앉으세요 (please sit), 기다려 주세요 (please wait), 문을 열어 주세요 (please open the door).

invitations.title: Making plans together
invitations.concept: 같이 (together) invites someone: 같이 가요. 갈래요? asks “Do you want to go?” and 시간 있어요? asks “Do you have time?”

signs.title: Signs you will see
signs.concept: Short signs are everywhere in Korea. **입구** is the entrance, **출구** the exit and **화장실** the restroom. On doors, **미세요** means push and **당기세요** means pull.

culture.title: Thank you for the meal
culture.concept: Before a meal say **잘 먹겠습니다**, and when you finish say **잘 먹었습니다**. A host welcomes you with **어서 오세요**, and **맛있어요** praises the food.

messages.title: Texting a friend
messages.concept: Text messages use short polite sentences ending in **-요**. **지금 어디예요?** asks where you are, **곧 가요** means “I’m coming soon” and **늦어요** means “I’m late”.

sounds.title: Reading words aloud
sounds.concept: When a syllable ends in a consonant and the next one starts with a vowel, the sound moves over: 책이 is read **chaegi** and 밥을 is read **babeul**. Some sounds also change their neighbours: 국물 is read **gungmul** and 같이 is read **gachi**.

indirect_state.title: Indirect statements (-다고 하다)
indirect_state.concept: Report what someone says or said: verb/adj + -다고 하다.

indirect_cmd.title: Indirect commands and suggestions (-라고 / -자고 하다)
indirect_cmd.concept: Report an imperative (-라고 하다) or propositive (-자고 하다).

cause_contrast.title: Complex causes and contrasts (-느라고, -는데도)
cause_contrast.concept: Negative cause or delay (-느라고) and contrast despite circumstances (-는데도).

proportion.title: Proportion and inevitability (-을수록, -기 마련이다)
proportion.concept: The more... the more (-을수록) and natural inevitability (-기 마련이다).

appearance.title: Appearance and inference (-아/어 보이다, -는 모양이다)
appearance.concept: Looks like (-아/어 보이다) and appears to be (-는 모양이다).

pretense.title: Pretending (-는 척하다)
pretense.concept: Pretend to do or be something: -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다.

regret.title: Regret and counterfactuals (-(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬어요)
regret.concept: Express regret: 'I should have done...' -(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬어요.

review_k7.title: K7 Comprehensive Review
review_k7.concept: Review indirect speech, complex connectors and nuanced expressions.

honorific_subj.title: Honorific vocabulary for subjects
honorific_subj.concept: Special honorific nouns and verbs for revered people: 진지, 주무시다, 편찮으시다.

honorific_obj.title: Object honorific verbs (드리다, 뵙다, 여쭙다)
honorific_obj.concept: Humble/honorific verbs when the action is directed toward an elder: 드리다, 뵙다, 여쭙다.

passive_affix.title: Affix passives (-이/히/리/기-)
passive_affix.concept: Passive verbs formed by adding -이/히/리/기-: 보이다, 들리다, 열리다, 닫히다.

passive_compound.title: Syntactic passives (-어지다, -게 되다)
passive_compound.concept: Verbs taking spontaneous or resulting passive forms: -아/어지다, -게 되다.

causative_affix.title: Affix causatives (-이/히/리/기/우-)
causative_affix.concept: Causative verbs that make someone do an action: 보여 주다, 먹이다, 입히다.

causative_compound.title: Syntactic causatives (-게 하다)
causative_compound.concept: Make or cause someone to do something: -게 하다.

formal_style.title: Public formal style (-하십시오)
formal_style.concept: High formal deferential style for announcements and ceremonies: -하십시오, -하십시다.

modesty.title: Modest and humble expressions
modesty.concept: Polite speech using humble pronouns and verbs: 저희, 말씀 올리다.

review_k8.title: K8 Comprehensive Review
review_k8.concept: Review honorifics, passive, causative and formal polite registers.

biz_email.title: Business email writing and requests
biz_email.concept: Formal business email conventions: -에 관하여, 검토 부탁드립니다.

biz_phone.title: Business telephone etiquette
biz_phone.concept: Handling calls and messages: 통화 가능하신지요, 연결해 드리겠습니다.

biz_schedule.title: Scheduling and rescheduling
biz_schedule.concept: Proposing and changing appointment times: 변경하고자 합니다, 양해 부탁드립니다.

biz_meeting.title: Meeting discussions and opinions
biz_meeting.concept: Expressing views during meetings: 제 생각으로는, 찬성합니다, 추가 검토.

biz_report.title: Reporting project progress
biz_report.concept: Giving status updates: 진행 상황을 보고합니다, 조치를 완료했습니다.

biz_stats.title: Statistical figures and data trends
biz_stats.concept: Describing trends and numbers: 증가했습니다, 전년 대비.

biz_negotiate.title: Business negotiations and partnerships
biz_negotiate.concept: Professional collaboration: 상호 협력을 희망합니다, 절충안 제시.

biz_etiquette.title: Business cards and professional titles
biz_etiquette.concept: Exchanging cards and titles: 처음 뵙겠습니다, 명함 드립니다.

review_k9.title: K9 Comprehensive Review
review_k9.concept: Review professional communications, formal correspondence and meetings.

media_headline.title: Headlines and compressed style
media_headline.concept: News headlines and compressed noun phrases: 물가 안정 대책 발표.

media_article.title: Current affairs and editorials
media_article.concept: Reading short news articles: 친환경 에너지가 주목받고 있습니다.

idioms_body.title: Body-part idioms (발, 눈, 귀, 손)
idioms_body.concept: Common idioms with body parts: 발이 넓다 (wide network), 눈이 높다 (high standards).

idioms_action.title: Everyday action idioms (바가지, 어깨)
idioms_action.concept: Expressions for common situations: 바가지를 쓰다 (ripped off), 어깨가 무겁다 (heavy duty).

proverbs_life.title: Essential Korean proverbs
proverbs_life.concept: Wisdom in proverbs: 소 잃고 외양간 고친다, 쇠뿔도 단김에 빼라.

sino_four.title: Four-character idioms (사자성어)
sino_four.concept: Common four-character Chinese-derived idioms: 일석이조, 작심삼일, 다다익선.

logic_debate.title: Logical connectors and discourse markers
logic_debate.concept: Formal discourse markers: -에 따르면, 한편, 요컨대, 따라서.

culture_deep.title: Deep Korean cultural values and customs
culture_deep.concept: Cultural concepts and holiday traditions: 따뜻한 정, 송편을 빚다.

review_k10.title: K10 Comprehensive Review
review_k10.concept: Mastery of Korean culture, media, idioms and formal debate expressions.
